Q: BCP Login failed for user A:

Try explicitly specifying the Server Name, User Name and Password.

exec master.dbo.xp_cmdshell 'bcp "select top 10 ProductFamilyID,ProductSetID,ProductFamilyCode,ProductFamilyName from MPLA.dbo.tblLCFProductFamily" queryout D:\requirement.txt -w -T -S YourServerName -U UserName -P Password'

Q: Excel SetFocus on Barcode Textbox -Not working A:

This works for me:

Private Sub TextBox1_Change()
    Const ENTER_TXT As String = vbCrLf '<< whatever your scanner sends
                                       '  to indicate "done"
    
    Static SKIP As Boolean 'flag to prevent triggering any action when
                           '  resetting the value
    Dim txt As String, bc As String
    
    If SKIP Then Exit Sub
    txt = TextBox1.Text

    If Right(txt, Len(ENTER_TXT)) = ENTER_TXT Then 'got a terminating key sequence?
        bc = Left(txt, Len(txt) - Len(ENTER_TXT))
        Me.HandleBarcode bc
        SKIP = True  'set the flag
        TextBox1.Text = bc
        TextBox1.SelStart = 0
        TextBox1.SelLength = Len(bc)
        SKIP = False 'clear the flag
    End If

End Sub

'check the barcode to see if we need to take any action
Sub HandleBarcode(bc As String)
    With Me.TextBox2
        Select Case bc
            Case "AAA"
                .BackColor = vbGreen
                .Text = "good"
            Case "BBB"
                .BackColor = vbRed
                .Text = "bad"
            Case Else
                .BackColor = vbWhite
                .Text = ""
        End Select
    End With
End Sub

As noted in the post I linked in a comment, you need to make sure to set the relevant properties on the textbox you want to use as the target for your scanner:

  • EnterKeyBehavior: True
  • Multiline: True

Figure out what sequence your scanner sends as a terminating "end of barcode" signal, and set ENTER_TEXT to that.

Q: Boomi HTTP Callout works in request phase but not response phase (Gravitee 3.3.13) A:

It’s not a Gravitee limitation. It’s a Boomi APIM UI limitation.

The Boomi UI does not allow creating an HTTP Callout policy in the response phase, so the callout never executes.

Workaround:
Create the HTTP Callout policy using Boomi’s internal GraphQL API instead of the UI. When created via GraphQL, the response-phase callout works correctly and the external API is invoked

Q: LINQPad 6 - change Temp directory with another one A:

Years later after this was first asked, I'm still running Linqpad 5 (due to maintaining legacy .NET Framework apps) and ran into this same issue. For anyone using Linqpad 5 and later (I've tested this on Linqpad 8 and it works as well), there is a setting you can configure to 'Run each query in its own process'. Go to Edit > Preferences > Advanced, then look under the subheading 'Execution':

Turn this setting off:

And Linqpad will stop creating exe files in temporary file locations in the current user's %appdata% folder. While you can't change the execution folder itself, this does get around the no-execution security policies that many corporate environments have in place, and the query will run inside the same Linqpad process, wherever it may be located (presumably it's already being executed inside a safe or excluded location).

Q: Safari Web inspector is blank A:

iOS 16.4+ requires isInspectable = true to allow Safari Web Inspector to connect.

In my case, I had a race condition setting isInspectable. The flag was set asynchronously in a SwiftUI .task modifier, so the WKWebView was created before the flag was set to true. Using a _queue.sync block in a setter solved the issue.

Force-setting/hardcoding this to true could be a useful tool in debugging this problem, for posterity.
